doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Choosing bandmates and laughing at failed ideas
summary: She picks flexible, listening musicians, and laughs at herself when an improvised idea fails.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Do you choose your band members and accompanists with that in mind? Like these particular players are most likely to help me get to those moments of truth?

Yes and no. The thought is not they’re going to help me get to the moment of truth, it’s more of like there are people that, with a sense of exploration with a level of listening and respect, and a lever of creativity that is going to challenge but not over bury. So it’s like the musicians that I choose, okay, I like flexible musicians that can go with the moment and not say oh I only know one thing so that’s what I’m going to play.
What would you do if you played something during an improvised solo that you didn’t like?

I’ll tell you what I do, I laugh. You would watch me often, I laugh at myself loudly in front of everybody. I don’t care. I mean because the experiment is I want to try and I’m like, wow that was a bad idea I don’t know what you were thinking. No. That ain’t gonna happen, that did not work. So sometimes it makes me laugh with like the chutzpah that I have to try something like that.
